status_rule: Initial statuses are immutable provenance. Read live BUILD state in build_map.md and live INFERENCE state in design/program/INFERENCE_IDEAS.md. Never dispatch from initial_status.

tasks.title: One pilot: deliberate device takeover without competing helm inputs
tasks.distinct_delta: The prior focus-loss packets clear held controls. This packet covers two simultaneously connected devices, pad-slot reuse and deliberate takeover while the window stays focused.
mechanism: Keep a single active movement-intent source in the existing input owner; meaningful movement or a deliberate action can take ownership, but sub-deadzone pad noise cannot.
On active-device loss, clear only its held intents and retain the current flight mode. Require a new deliberate input before another connected pad acquires control.
Route pointer, pad and touch intents through the same action merge and preserve independent aim/fire semantics; UI activity must not silently retake the helm.
tasks.route: Normal flight, seed 4242: use the G stick, connect a drifting pad, deliberately take over, unplug it during a tow, then resume on the pointer.
acceptance: A neutral or noisy unused pad never changes the commanded flight vector.
A disconnected device contributes zero held actions on the next input sample; another device works without restarting.
Each deliberate takeover produces one action-source change and no duplicate bomb, shot or Massline edge.
tasks.non_goals: Do not retune thrust, impose new velocity damping, add a second input manager, or assume pad array indexes are persistent identities.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Ignore neutral noise from the unused pad
tasks.change: Exclude sub-deadzone axes from the existing last-active-device decision, without changing the configured flight deadzone.
tasks.acceptance: A centered second pad cannot replace a pointer-authored vector across 600 samples; a deliberate axis movement still registers.
tasks.forbidden: Do not increase every device deadzone to hide drift.

tasks.title: Clear disconnect edges rather than replaying them
tasks.change: On disconnect discard the removed pad's cached pressed/released buttons and axes.
tasks.acceptance: Unplug while holding fire and reconnect at the reused index: no inherited shot or held thrust occurs before new input.
tasks.forbidden: Do not clear keyboard state or reset the ship.

tasks.title: Show the newly active control family once
tasks.change: Reflect the accepted input source in the existing controls surface, using the parent source result rather than independent pointer-hover detection.
tasks.acceptance: One deliberate source switch changes the displayed control family once; hovering Settings does not change the in-flight source.
tasks.forbidden: Do not add a persistent flight toast.

tasks.title: Keep two gamepads distinguishable after index reuse
tasks.change: Use the parent takeover record to reject cached input from a disconnected connection generation when its array slot is reused.
tasks.acceptance: Pad A disconnects; pad B occupies its slot with different bindings; only B's fresh mapping is accepted.
tasks.forbidden: Do not persist a browser hardware fingerprint.

tasks.title: Keep the G-stick response stable through resize, zoom and display-density changes
tasks.distinct_delta: The current stick already projects through the live camera and snapshots recycled ray results. The remaining contract here is device/viewport calibration during an active gesture, not rebuilding that projection.
mechanism: At a viewport/radius change preserve the normalized virtual-knob displacement, not the old pixel distance, then apply the existing response curve.
Keep CSS-pixel input and raycast coordinates in one declared space; device-pixel ratio affects backing buffers, not commanded thrust.
Exercise the live camera basis at ordinary chase zooms and retain the existing fail-closed result for an invalid ray; a recovery must use the current gesture rather than a stale world vector.
tasks.route: Normal G flight with a half-deflected stick: resize the window, change OS/browser display scale, zoom the camera, and repeat while towing.
acceptance: At unchanged normalized displacement, commanded magnitude agrees before/after resize within numerical tolerance.
A display-density change alone does not rotate or amplify intent.
At the clamp boundary, inward motion immediately reduces intent; invalid projection yields no non-finite command.
tasks.non_goals: Do not replace the G stick with draw-to-fly, add target homing, or retune propulsion to compensate for input scaling.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Preserve a neutral stick when the viewport collapses
tasks.change: Treat zero-sized/minimized viewports as non-commanding rather than manufacturing a large normalized gesture.
tasks.acceptance: Minimize at neutral and restore: zero thrust until actual input; all intermediate outputs are finite.
tasks.forbidden: Do not store a fabricated player position.

tasks.title: Reject an absurd pointer packet without discarding the gesture
tasks.change: Keep the existing corrupt-packet rejection atomic: invalid deltas cannot partially mutate knob position or radius.
tasks.acceptance: A valid half-stick followed by an oversized or NaN packet projects identically to the pre-packet state.
tasks.forbidden: Do not lower sensitivity for normal fast swipes.

tasks.title: Rescale an active knob once per viewport revision
tasks.change: Use the parent normalized-radius transfer for a mid-gesture resize; avoid applying the ratio again on subsequent packets.
tasks.acceptance: Two identical resize notifications followed by zero motion preserve the same half-stick magnitude.
tasks.forbidden: Do not accumulate resize compensation every frame.

tasks.title: Return the G-stick indicator to the real normalized vector
tasks.change: Where the current instrument exposes G-mode activity, consume the authoritative active/magnitude result rather than infer it from auto-fire being enabled.
tasks.acceptance: G enabled at neutral is shown as enabled but not actively steering; nonzero intent and return-to-neutral are truthful.
tasks.forbidden: Do not invent a new speed gauge or joystick chrome.

tasks.title: Make simultaneous input edges mean the same thing at different render rates
tasks.distinct_delta: The prior packet addresses one input edge during frame debt. This expands the defined ordering to simultaneous context-sensitive verbs and press/release pairs without changing the fixed-step loop.
mechanism: Record action edges with their input-sample order and consume each once at the existing simulation boundary.

Define conflict precedence in the current input grammar: a contextual UI capture consumes its key; a Massline release does not also relatch; shared detonate targets the already-armed set at consumption time.
Replay the same sampled input schedule under 30/60/120-Hz presentation and bounded catch-up; do not derive action counts from the number of rendered frames.
tasks.route: Fly the normal Crucible route: press and release tether rapidly, drop then detonate ordnance, and open/close a modal in the same render interval.
acceptance: The same sample sequence yields the same action counts and authoritative outcomes across presentation schedules.
A press and release arriving before a render are not silently lost or converted into an indefinite hold.
Captured UI input never leaks into a later flight step after closing the modal.
tasks.non_goals: Do not add a second simulation loop, cap legitimate sim debt to hide ordering errors, or rewrite replay goldens without a causal record.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Ignore browser key-repeat for edge-only verbs

tasks.acceptance: A held deploy key produces one deploy edge; held movement still lasts until release.
tasks.forbidden: Do not globally discard held input.

tasks.title: Consume a captured Escape without dropping a bomb
tasks.change: Consume the close/cancel event in the existing topmost UI handler, including its paired release where needed.
tasks.acceptance: Closing a screen with a remapped key does not also invoke its in-flight binding.
tasks.forbidden: Do not disable every flight key permanently when a screen closes.

tasks.title: Order release before a new latch on a single sampled transition

tasks.acceptance: Two successive sampled edges yield one release and one new latch, never two live ropes for the same slot.
tasks.forbidden: Do not add an arbitrary multi-frame input lockout.

tasks.title: Keep edge timestamps out of wall-clock gameplay decisions
tasks.change: Use the parent sample/tick sequence for edge ordering; browser timestamps may remain diagnostics only.
tasks.acceptance: Replaying with different wall-clock offsets leaves verb ordering unchanged.
tasks.forbidden: Do not alter the save checksum or canonical serializer.

tasks.title: A damaged loaded ship remains controllable through the real propulsion stack
tasks.distinct_delta: Loaded handling and side-shove control are already separate plans. This is their combined boundary with subsystem damage, a tether load and repaired propulsion, not another universal flight tune.
mechanism: Trace achieved thrust and torque through flightV3, propulsionKernel and combat subsystem effects for one light and one cargo hull.
Preserve external impulse and attached mass; expose the actual remaining authority so braking and steering are limited by the existing machinery rather than hidden assist compensation.
Repair the first mismatched authority or stale derived-stat handoff, then prove that repair restores only the damaged capability and does not reset momentum.
tasks.route: Load a normal cargo hull, sustain engine/subsystem damage in adventure, tow a body out of danger, release it, repair at a station and fly the same turn.
acceptance: Damage changes the correct available force/torque channel, not unrelated input magnitude.
Release or repair causes no unexplained pose/velocity discontinuity.
The light and loaded hull remain distinguishable and each responds to deliberate steering throughout the recovery route.
tasks.non_goals: No direct pos/vel writes from flight helpers, compensating NPC/player gyros, flat speed nerf, or free repair on docking.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Display unavailable thrust as unavailable, not idle
tasks.change: Distinguish requested thrust, achieved thrust and a disabled drive in the existing telemetry projection.
tasks.acceptance: A held throttle on a disabled drive never reports healthy zero-effort coasting as the cause.
tasks.forbidden: Do not write combat subsystem state from telemetry.

tasks.title: Refresh handling after an accepted cargo removal
tasks.change: Ensure the accepted mass change invalidates the existing derived handling cache once, including partial removal.
tasks.acceptance: Removing half a dense cargo lot changes usedMass and the next handling read consistently; rejected removal changes neither.
tasks.forbidden: Do not introduce mass as a second hard cargo capacity.

tasks.title: Release a damaged tow without restoring healthy drive stats
tasks.change: Retain the parent damaged propulsion availability when the attachment load disappears.
tasks.acceptance: A cut changes the attachment load but the disabled subsystem remains disabled.
tasks.forbidden: Do not normalize to the hull catalog on every release.

tasks.title: Repair telemetry keeps its before-and-after basis
tasks.change: Expose the repaired channel in the same unit/basis used for its damaged value, so the existing instrument can compare it without a cosmetic rescale.
tasks.acceptance: A repair changes achieved authority, not the scale denominator or requested-input readout.
tasks.forbidden: Do not add a second hull-health meter.

tasks.title: A recovered tow reaches a receiver with its custody and value intact
tasks.distinct_delta: Earlier packets establish salvage sorting, split custody and interrupted transfer separately. This packet completes a recovered enemy/civilian load through release, relatch, receiver acceptance and settlement.
mechanism: Use the current stable world/cargo record as the identity across wreck, loose payload, tether target and receiver input.
Receiver acceptance transfers only accepted quantity and the corresponding provenance; the remainder stays a ropeable physical load.
Route salvage entitlement, credits and cargo to their canonical owners after acceptance, rather than infer ownership from whoever is currently tethering the body.
tasks.route: From the adventure opening, recover a raid spill, lose and regain the latch, bring it to a partly full receiver, and return for the remainder.
acceptance: Total accepted, remaining and destroyed quantity reconciles to the starting lot.
Tethering alone never changes legal ownership or mints salvage value.
Saving before the final acceptance and resuming neither duplicates payment nor erases the remaining body.
tasks.non_goals: Do not rebuild cargo custody or receiver systems already owned by the prior packets; no delivery by invisible proximity credit.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: A latched payload remains selectable during a partial unload
tasks.change: Keep selection bound to the surviving stable load record when a receiver accepts only part of a payload.
tasks.acceptance: Partial acceptance leaves one valid target; full acceptance cleanly releases it.
tasks.forbidden: Do not create a replacement full-size duplicate pod.

tasks.title: Reject zero-unit receiver acceptance as a delivery
tasks.change: Only emit successful delivery/operation completion for a positive accepted material quantity.
tasks.acceptance: A full receiver produces a refusal result and no success credit.
tasks.forbidden: Do not force the receiver to accept beyond its capacity.

tasks.title: Explain recovered versus stolen freight at the handover
tasks.change: Use the parent custody result to show the applicable disposition on the existing selected-lot detail before settlement.
tasks.acceptance: Two identical commodities with different custody have different truthful disposition text.
tasks.forbidden: Do not turn every legal distinction into a new commodity ID.

tasks.title: Keep the residual load name after the first delivery
tasks.change: Carry the parent origin/display identity onto the remaining quantity after an accepted split.
tasks.acceptance: The remainder is still identifiable as the same recovered shipment, not an anonymous generic pickup.
tasks.forbidden: Do not serialize UI nodes or duplicate narrative prose per unit.

tasks.title: Transfer a load across a moving industrial gap without scripted motion
tasks.distinct_delta: Anchor swapping and industrial bypasses exist as separate directions. The selected extension is one moving-gap handoff that exercises both, with no new rope solver or fake payload path.
mechanism: Choose one existing moving receiver/worksite and use its real cycle as the opportunity window.
Permit a payload already manipulated through Massline to enter the receiver's actual swept acceptance geometry; a miss remains ordinary moving freight.
Teach the usable interval through the machine's own motion and contact surfaces, with a clear recovery apron instead of a tutorial modal or magnetic snap.
tasks.route: At a currently reachable industrial site, observe one cycle, throw a load through the opening, miss the next throw, then recover it from the apron.
acceptance: At least one successful and one failed release resolve from the same collision/acceptance rules.
Machine movement changes the available gap without teleporting the payload.
A missed load remains recoverable and does not jam progress permanently or reset the site.
tasks.non_goals: No new encounter clone if an existing site already owns the beat; no auto-guided throw, position animation of the payload, or new one-off physics.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: A closed intake says closed rather than invalid target

tasks.forbidden: Do not extend the opening window as a UI fix.

tasks.title: Do not offer a scripted machine proxy as a dynamic tow body
tasks.change: Apply the existing physicsBody:false exclusion consistently to the advertised acquisition result.
tasks.acceptance: A kinematic machine proxy is not offered as throwable cargo; an actual loose payload beside it is.
tasks.forbidden: Do not convert all machinery to dynamic physics bodies.

tasks.title: Distinguish lip contact from successful entry
tasks.change: Map the parent receiver's contact result to the existing feedback event without accepting material on the wrong side of the lip.
tasks.acceptance: A glancing lip collision produces contact feedback but no delivered quantity.
tasks.forbidden: Do not add an invisible enlarged success radius.

tasks.title: A recovered miss remains eligible for the next cycle
tasks.change: Clear only the completed attempt marker when the same load is recovered and thrown again.
tasks.acceptance: A first miss followed by a valid second entry can succeed once.
tasks.forbidden: Do not reset material damage or provenance on retry.

tasks.title: One physical kill has one readable legal and salvage aftermath
tasks.distinct_delta: This is not another stunt detector. It joins throw provenance, chained collision damage, legal attribution and the resulting salvage claim when more than one actor supplied momentum.
mechanism: Carry the existing causal root and immediate contributor through release and collision events, retaining bounded attribution rather than the whole collision graph.
Choose a stable attribution rule at the damage/impulse owner: the immediate damage cause and the responsible actor remain separate facts.
Law, salvage and the existing stunt receipt consume those same facts; never let a renderer effect or a last-hit UI guess determine responsibility.
tasks.route: Throw a hostile into a civilian pod and a second hostile, then repeat after an NPC changes the thrown body's momentum. Inspect the ensuing loss, wreck and legal response.
acceptance: Every destroyed body settles once even if multiple damage events arrive in the same tick.
Civilian damage, player credit and recovered ownership all cite compatible causal facts.
An unrelated late nudge cannot erase the original evidence or claim an entire chain without the adopted attribution rule.
tasks.non_goals: No new global karma system, combo multiplier, duplicate damage router, or omniscient witness.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Do not label a natural collision as a player throw
tasks.change: Retain an explicit absence of responsible actor when no valid recent impulse provenance exists.
tasks.acceptance: An unowned drifting rock collision never receives the player ID merely because the player is nearest.
tasks.forbidden: Do not disable environmental collision damage.

tasks.title: Break equal-tick attribution ties stably
tasks.change: Resolve equivalent causal candidates using existing stable entity/event ordering rather than Map visitation accidents.
tasks.acceptance: Reordered presentation/entity views do not change responsibility for the same ordered sim inputs.
tasks.forbidden: Do not sort or mutate the authoritative entity store globally.

tasks.title: Use the immediate cause in the existing aftermath sentence
tasks.change: Keep the parent legal owner separate from the displayed physical cause so a thrown-body collision is not renamed a gun kill.
tasks.acceptance: The receipt names the physical move while the law result retains its own responsible actor.
tasks.forbidden: Do not add a second result toast.

tasks.title: Remove dead attribution roots at the established expiry

tasks.acceptance: Repeated chains reach a stable retained-record count; unsettled outcomes are not removed early.
tasks.forbidden: Do not truncate still-relevant legal evidence to hit a memory target.

tasks.title: Recover a volatile load by managing its physical exposure, not a scripted timer
tasks.distinct_delta: The opening already has volatile cargo. This packet makes the player's route, impacts and nearby hazards matter during an actual recovery, using the existing heat/damage model rather than adding another bomb type.
mechanism: Bind one existing volatile shipment to its current damage/thermal exposure facts and preserve them through towing, cutting and repickup.
Give the selected route one meaningful cool/sheltered continuation and one faster hazardous continuation using existing geometry or fields.
A successful delivery settles its remaining usable material; rupture spills or destroys the appropriate fraction through ordinary cargo/destruction owners.
tasks.route: Recover the existing opening volatile freight; take the sheltered way once and the risky shortcut once, including a recoverable glancing collision.
acceptance: The two routes change actual exposure/contact outcomes, not a hidden mission success variable.
Relatching, docking refusal or saving does not cool or heal the load for free.
At least one imperfect recovery still yields usable freight instead of binary arbitrary failure.
tasks.non_goals: No new global temperature simulator, unavoidable countdown, tow-immunity flag, or changed cargo economy unrelated to this load.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Keep volatile identity through jettison and recovery
tasks.change: Preserve the existing commodity and volatility metadata when a held lot becomes a physical pod.
tasks.acceptance: The same known volatile lot remains volatile after dump and pickup; inert cargo remains inert.
tasks.forbidden: Do not mark all freight explosive.

tasks.title: Show condition without promising a countdown

tasks.title: Allow salvage of the useful fraction after a partial rupture

Apply the accepted order through existing bomb and economy owners as one coherent transaction; rejected or stale terms leave the prior rack and credits intact.
Return units displaced by a smaller rack to owned stock, and retain fitted payload identity in empty cells rather than replacing the player's preparation choice.
tasks.route: At an ordinary outfitting berth, partially restock two bomb families with insufficient credits, change hull/socket count and then undock.
acceptance: Every loaded unit is accounted for by prior rack, owned stock or paid accepted purchase.
Preview and committed quantity agree or the existing confirmation is explicitly refreshed.
Repeated confirm, cancel and retry cannot double-charge, mint ammunition or discard displaced rounds.

tasks.title: Keep a dry fitted cell named in the rack readout

tasks.title: Retain selection when the chosen family is successfully refilled

tasks.acceptance: A partial restock does not silently switch the next dropped bomb to a different family.
tasks.forbidden: Do not reorder all rack cells by price or damage.

tasks.title: Overlapping fields produce a predictable net force without stealing the controls
tasks.distinct_delta: Prior plans make individual fields readable. This work fixes the compositional law for simultaneous pull, push and viscosity on moving bodies, especially equal/opposed fields and kinematic exclusions.
mechanism: At the current force owner, resolve the existing fields against the same pre-step body state and submit their combined force/impulse through physicsAuthority.
Keep viscosity dissipative relative to its authored moving field, while pull/push remain their actual vector effects; do not emulate any of these by setting a body velocity.
Preserve projectile/bomb ownership and kinematic exclusions, and let the current force-language renderer show the contributors without inventing a second physics calculation.
tasks.route: In a normal Crucible round, overlap an existing well, repulsor and viscous bomb around moving loose cargo and both a light and heavy hostile.
acceptance: Reordering equivalent field enumeration does not alter the authoritative outcome beyond the existing deterministic convention.
A stationary dissipative field cannot add kinetic energy solely through its viscosity term.
Equal opposing fields may cancel their force while player steering and external momentum remain intact.
tasks.non_goals: No global velocity clamp, hard stun, per-render force application, or new field system beside fields/bombs.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Exclude kinematic bodies consistently from field drag
tasks.change: Use the existing dynamic-body predicate for viscous field effects, not a ship-type shortcut.
tasks.acceptance: A physicsBody:false scripted proxy keeps its owner's motion; a real dynamic cargo body receives the effect.
tasks.forbidden: Do not turn the exclusion into immunity for ordinary heavy hulls.

tasks.title: A field at exact zero range produces finite output
tasks.change: Handle coincident field/body centers with the existing deterministic zero-direction convention.
tasks.acceptance: Center overlap never creates NaN impulse, teleportation or an arbitrary unseeded direction.
tasks.forbidden: Do not move the body away to avoid division by zero.

tasks.title: Preserve the sign of the combined force readout
tasks.change: Consume the parent resolved contribution so a net push is not displayed as a pull merely because a well is present.
tasks.acceptance: Opposed-field cases display the accepted net effect and retain contributor identity where already supported.
tasks.forbidden: Do not recompute physics from rendered positions.

tasks.title: Do not leave a viscous status after the field is gone
tasks.change: Remove only the expired parent field's contribution; another live viscosity source may remain.
tasks.acceptance: Exiting one of two overlapping sources removes one contribution without erasing or multiplying the other.
tasks.forbidden: Do not clear all combat statuses as cleanup.

Stage one ordinary combat opportunity with a safe disposal direction; the resulting blast still uses real geometry and collateral rules.

A player can learn one reliable counter from the visible armed/body/impact states without a debug overlay.

acceptance: One accepted use consumes the authored quantity once and affects only eligible lock lineages.

Reacquisition needs the current allowed observation and cannot come from a recycled target ID.

tasks.forbidden: Do not make the player globally invisible.

tasks.title: A stale target generation cannot inherit a reacquisition
tasks.change: Validate the parent target generation at reacquisition/commit, even if an entity ID has been reused.
tasks.acceptance: A newly spawned body at an old ID is not automatically locked by yesterday's missile.
tasks.forbidden: Do not rebuild the entire targeting registry.

tasks.title: A wounded squad withdraws through a usable corridor with one covering ship
tasks.distinct_delta: Individual retreat, shared perception and obstacle avoidance already have owners. This packet specifies their group handoff: a wounded member leaves while a healthy member covers, without every ship oscillating between attack and flee.
mechanism: Choose a retreat corridor from currently perceived navigable space and keep it for a bounded commitment unless physically invalidated.
Assign one eligible covering member through the existing squad decision; it pressures the pursuer while the wounded member obeys normal inertia, clearance and escape rules.
End cover when the retreat succeeds, the coverer is disabled or the corridor becomes invalid; reacquire a current plan rather than preserving a stale target.
tasks.route: Damage one member of an ordinary multi-ship encounter near cover, pursue it, then disable the covering member or obstruct the intended exit.
acceptance: The wounded ship makes observable progress toward an escape instead of endless spin or mode-flipping.
A single eligible coverer takes the role; no squad-wide omniscience or instantaneous formation teleport occurs.
Blocking the route produces a finite replanning response while normal collisions and player counterplay remain.
tasks.non_goals: No new behavior-tree framework, universal retreat speed buff, direct pose writes or hidden invulnerability during disengagement.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: A destroyed leader cannot remain the retreat anchor
tasks.change: Reject a dead or invalid-generation leader when deriving the existing shared retreat target.
tasks.acceptance: Destroy the leader between perception updates: followers do not steer toward a recycled ID.
tasks.forbidden: Do not dissolve every squad whenever its leader changes.

tasks.title: Bound a stationary retreat deadlock before reselection
tasks.change: Use the existing stationary/deadlock state to invalidate an unreachable retreat corridor instead of repeatedly selecting its same blocked waypoint.
tasks.acceptance: A blocked retreat makes a different legal choice within the configured deadlock horizon.
tasks.forbidden: Do not increase retreat speed to tunnel through the obstacle.

tasks.title: Release the covering assignment when its ward escapes
tasks.change: Clear the parent cover role on the ward's actual departure or accepted escape result.
tasks.acceptance: A covering ship returns to an appropriate live plan rather than guarding an empty coordinate forever.
tasks.forbidden: Do not despawn the coverer.

tasks.title: Signal the commitment with one existing doctrine cue
tasks.change: Emit the parent retreat-cover state transition through the existing doctrine cue path only when the commitment changes.
tasks.acceptance: One cover assignment gives one cue, not a cue per decision tick.
tasks.forbidden: Do not write new radio dialogue or add an alert channel.

tasks.title: Lawful combat stands down when the specific surrender is accepted
tasks.distinct_delta: Customs crossings and surrender already exist. The missing proof target here is the cross-owner boundary between accepted compliance and queued AI fire/ordnance, including a different lawful officer arriving later.
mechanism: Trace the existing surrender/impound result into fresh engagementAuthority checks, not just the current squad's advisory target.
Cancel uncommitted attacks that are no longer authorized while retaining already-fired physical projectiles and truthful consequences.
Make a later lawful unit consult the current local disposition; a new unrelated crime may reopen engagement through the normal authority, not a permanent mercy flag.
tasks.route: On an ordinary customs route, surrender the relevant freight during a telegraphed attack, then let a second patrol observe the scene. Repeat after committing a new hostile act.
acceptance: After accepted surrender, no newly committed unauthorized shot leaves a lawful ship.
Already-fired ordnance is neither silently erased nor relabeled as a fresh lawful decision.
New misconduct can be recognized without resurrecting the settled accusation or applying it twice.
tasks.non_goals: No blanket immunity, raw reputation-based shoot flag, team reassignment hack or deletion of flying ordnance.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Recheck authority immediately before a queued shot commits
tasks.change: Keep the final execution path on the current engagement-authority result, even when advisory intent was produced earlier.
tasks.acceptance: A compliance change between decision and execution prevents a newly unauthorized shot.
tasks.forbidden: Do not bypass response-window or jurisdiction checks.

tasks.title: Keep local warrant resolution separate from global heat
tasks.change: Resolve only the identified local disposition on accepted compliance; unrelated active causes remain.
tasks.acceptance: Settling one inspection does not erase another valid offense or restart the settled one.
tasks.forbidden: Do not zero all player heat as a surrender implementation.

tasks.title: Describe stand-down using the accepted disposition
tasks.change: Send the parent settled/suspended distinction through the existing lawful response message.
tasks.acceptance: A provisional stop is not announced as complete legal exoneration.
tasks.forbidden: Do not add a new reputation reward.

tasks.title: Do not reopen the same surrendered lot on a late arrival
tasks.change: Validate the parent settlement identity when a new lawful observer evaluates the same freight.
tasks.acceptance: A second patrol sees the accepted disposition but can still act on genuinely new contraband or aggression.
tasks.forbidden: Do not globally suppress all future inspections.

tasks.title: Convoys negotiate a narrow obstruction instead of shoving every member through it
tasks.distinct_delta: Berth queues and single-ship avoidance are existing work. This is one moving convoy at one narrow obstruction: ordered passage, an escort holding position and recovery when the player blocks the gap.
mechanism: Use the existing convoy/formation identity to select a stable passage order at a constrained segment.
Leading freight commits to the gap; following ships wait at physical stand-off points and the escort maintains a useful guarding position through the live maneuver owner.
If the gap stays blocked or a member is lost, release/recompute that local order without inventing an omniscient route or pinning the convoy forever.
tasks.route: Observe an existing hauler/escort group approaching a real narrow industrial route, obstruct it with a tow, then clear it and follow the convoy.
acceptance: The group passes without repeated collisions or all members choosing the same parking point.
The player can interrupt and release the flow through real geometry.
No waiting member freezes its simulation or loses its cargo/identity when the convoy reforms.
tasks.non_goals: No global traffic-light system, forced linear path animation, scripted teleport through the gap or extra ambient fleet.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Use hull clearance, not one shared point, for convoy stand-off
tasks.change: Offset existing waiting positions by the members' actual clearance envelopes and stable order.
tasks.acceptance: Two unequal hulls waiting behind a narrow gap do not overlap at a single anchor.
tasks.forbidden: Do not inflate every collision radius.

tasks.title: Drop a lost convoy member from the local wait condition
tasks.change: Remove a destroyed/departed member from the existing convoy completion predicate.
tasks.acceptance: The remaining convoy does not wait forever for an entity that cannot return.
tasks.forbidden: Do not delete the lost member's durable cargo/loss record.

tasks.title: Allow the player-cleared gap to release one committed member
tasks.change: Use the parent passage reservation to admit the next surviving member once the preceding envelope is clear.
tasks.acceptance: Clearing the obstacle starts a stable sequence rather than a simultaneous surge.
tasks.forbidden: Do not impose a fixed delay unrelated to geometry.

tasks.title: An escort keeps its guard target when the hauler pauses
tasks.change: Preserve the parent protected group/objective during a temporary local passage wait.
tasks.acceptance: A paused hauler does not cause its escort to abandon protection or attack a neutral blocker automatically.
tasks.forbidden: Do not equate obstruction with lawful hostility.

tasks.title: A capital opening follows a damaged physical subsystem rather than a health-bar phase
tasks.distinct_delta: Heavy hulls and boss rounds already exist. This packet selects one current capital attack whose vulnerability changes because a specific subsystem is disabled or reoriented by the player.
mechanism: Choose an existing capital and one actually modeled subsystem/attack capability; identify the physical disabling opportunity before adding any content.
Connect that accepted subsystem transition to a bounded tactical opening in the current decision/doctrine owner, while leaving the hull's inertia and remaining capabilities live.
Make recovery or adaptation follow the actual subsystem state; an alternative physical route must remain available to builds lacking the ideal disabling weapon.
tasks.route: Fight the selected capital on its existing ordinary mission/Crucible route. Open a window once by precision damage and once through a permitted physical collision or alternative attack.
acceptance: The opening starts only after the relevant accepted state change, not at an arbitrary global HP percentage.
The capital retains readable, constrained agency and can be exploited without being frozen.
A legal non-specialist build has a slower but viable response, with no required hidden equipment.
tasks.non_goals: No new boss framework, decorative weak point disconnected from damage, HP inflation, mandatory rare gear or cutscene movement.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: A disabled weapon subsystem cannot advertise ready fire
tasks.change: Make the existing readiness projection agree with the canonical disabled-subsystem result.
tasks.acceptance: A disabled bank neither commits a shot nor displays a healthy ready state.
tasks.forbidden: Do not silence healthy banks on the same hull.

tasks.title: Keep the capital silhouette targetable after subsystem damage
tasks.change: Preserve the hull's primary interaction identity when only a subsystem is disabled.
tasks.acceptance: The damaged capital remains targetable and physically collidable; only the intended capability changes.
tasks.forbidden: Do not turn subsystem failure into entity death.

tasks.title: Announce the real opening once per transition
tasks.change: Publish the parent vulnerable-state transition through the existing doctrine/cue path with a stable transition ID.
tasks.acceptance: Repeated damage while already open does not spam additional opening cues or rewards.
tasks.forbidden: Do not add a second boss health bar.

tasks.title: Close the opening on real recovery, not a presentation timeout
tasks.change: Use the parent accepted subsystem/recovery state to authorize the recovered attack.
tasks.acceptance: Slow-motion or a delayed VFX frame cannot extend or prematurely close the gameplay window.
tasks.forbidden: Do not let the renderer write attack authorization.

tasks.title: Author one three-round act whose physical question changes each round
tasks.distinct_delta: The old bank specifies individual good rounds. This is their composition into a short act: exploit a body, protect an opportunity, then apply the learned interaction under combined pressure.
mechanism: Select three adjacent existing act slots, not a new game mode. First make loose mass useful against an exposed enemy, then introduce one specialist that contests that use, then combine it with a heavy anchor and a clear counter-window.
Author ingress, spacing and available physical tools through the existing pure wave recipe, staying within its current spawn budgets.
Keep one genuine recovery/draft interval so the player can connect a fitting choice to the next problem; do not make each round merely a larger roster.
tasks.route: From normal Swarm selection, play the selected three-round segment on a starter-compatible build and a contrasting existing build.
acceptance: Each round has a different describable physical decision, not just a different enemy count.
Both builds can finish without a mandatory random draft result.
All phases terminate correctly if a key enemy is displaced, disabled or killed earlier than the expected order.
tasks.non_goals: No fourth progression mode, extra difficulty currency, hidden scripted kill requirement or higher simultaneous-body ceiling.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Preserve a useful opening lane in the chosen spawn recipe
tasks.change: For the selected existing recipe, keep one escape/approach lane outside the initial enemy envelope.
tasks.acceptance: The starter's spawn is not immediately enclosed on every side by the authored first package.
tasks.forbidden: Do not reduce all encounter counts globally.

tasks.title: Reject a recipe whose scheduled population exceeds its budget
tasks.change: Keep the existing peak-concurrent validation on composed packages, including delayed batches.
tasks.acceptance: An intentionally over-budget composed recipe returns a useful authoring error rather than silently dropping opponents.
tasks.forbidden: Do not clamp the roster after planning and call it the authored wave.

tasks.title: Name the next act question without prescribing the solution
tasks.change: Give the parent act's existing transition text one compact physical cue for the next round.
tasks.acceptance: The text distinguishes the three problems without telling the player a required exact combo.
tasks.forbidden: Do not open a tutorial modal between every round.

tasks.title: Keep the specialist introduction out of the later act reprise
tasks.change: Use the parent introduction marker to avoid repeating the first-time teaching interruption on a later remix.
tasks.acceptance: A repeated act can reuse the mechanic without replaying its introductory stop.
tasks.forbidden: Do not suppress mechanically necessary attack telegraphs.

tasks.title: Draft offers remain useful for the actual build and transaction state
tasks.distinct_delta: Draft fitting, refusal and run wallets already exist. The delta is offer generation and explanations for duplicate ownership, full slots, mutually exclusive fits and a changing run state.
mechanism: Derive candidate eligibility from the current ships/capability owner before presenting an offer, without fabricating temporary stats.
Keep sidegrades that require a known replacement, but state what leaves the fit and what remains owned; remove choices that cannot possibly apply.
At commit, revalidate the exact offer and settle once through existing draft/run requests; a changed fit may refresh or refuse, never silently buy a different benefit.
tasks.route: Reach an ordinary draft with a nearly full fit, existing duplicate equipment and an unusual build; make, skip and reroll choices through the normal surface.
acceptance: Every presented choice is applicable or has an explicit feasible replacement path.
The accepted result matches its actual fit/capability delta and charges only the run wallet.
A duplicate confirm or stale offer cannot grant a module twice or mutate the Adventure wallet.
tasks.non_goals: No free stat writes, guaranteed perfect counter-build, new rarity ladder or separate draft equipment owner.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: A refused draft has a terminal result
tasks.change: Ensure a denied fitting request leaves the existing draft in a retryable or skippable terminal state rather than pending forever.
tasks.acceptance: A full-slot refusal can be skipped or retried without duplicate charge.
tasks.forbidden: Do not force-fit the rejected equipment.

tasks.title: Do not offer an exact no-op duplicate as an upgrade
tasks.change: Exclude a candidate whose accepted ownership/fit effect is exactly empty, unless the current rules explicitly grant usable additional stock.
tasks.acceptance: An already-owned unique item is not sold again as an unqualified power increase.
tasks.forbidden: Do not ban stackable equipment that is actually useful.

tasks.title: State the displaced fitting in the offer description
tasks.change: Attach the parent replacement projection to the existing offer result.
tasks.acceptance: The player can distinguish adding a module from replacing the one currently enabling a tactic.
tasks.forbidden: Do not infer the lost capability from item flavor text.

tasks.title: Keep a declined offer out of the same reroll result
tasks.change: Use the parent deterministic offer history to avoid immediately presenting an identical declined set when alternatives exist.
tasks.acceptance: Same seed and history reproduce the same nonidentical feasible set; exhausted catalogs fail honestly.
tasks.forbidden: Do not draw from Math.random or invent unavailable items.

tasks.title: The arena carries useful physical history across preparation intervals
tasks.distinct_delta: Keeping grabbable wrecks into the next round is already directed work. This extension defines which player-changed arena facts persist across refits and how those facts remain useful without uncontrolled accumulation.
mechanism: Retain existing stable arena facts for displaced durable cover, selected surviving wreck resources and exhausted supplies across the current preparation transition.
Bound only replaceable presentation/debris through its established lifecycle; do not delete meaningful objects because a round number advanced.
When a recipe needs a guaranteed affordance, supply its existing authored replacement condition transparently rather than restoring the whole arena or moving player-owned wrecks.
tasks.route: In normal Swarm, move cover, spend a supply and keep a useful wreck; enter preparation, change equipment and play the next round in the same altered space.
acceptance: The next round preserves the named durable changes and does not regenerate consumed supplies.
The chosen act remains solvable after a player destroys or displaces optional cover.
Repeated rounds retain bounded disposable effects while meaningful retained facts are not silently culled.
tasks.non_goals: No persistent universe inside Swarm, generic arena reset after each wave or body deletion as a performance fix.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: A collected supply stays spent through refit
tasks.change: Use the current collected/consumed identity when preparation rebinds arena objects.
tasks.acceptance: Collect, refit and return: the same supply does not pay twice.
tasks.forbidden: Do not remove every uncollected supply at the phase change.

tasks.title: Count disabled survivors using the current round rule
tasks.change: Distinguish an alive but neutralized objective from a remaining actionable hostile using the existing wave completion contract.
tasks.acceptance: Disabling the last relevant attacker does not leave an impossible cleanup wait or falsely remove a still-dangerous opponent.
tasks.forbidden: Do not despawn the target to force a clear.

tasks.title: Preserve the player-moved cover transform across preparation
tasks.change: Use the parent durable arena record instead of an authored spawn transform when reattaching the same cover identity.
tasks.acceptance: Moved cover returns at its actual retained transform without a visible snap to its initial location.
tasks.forbidden: Do not serialize renderer matrices as gameplay truth.

tasks.title: Explain replenishment only when a real replacement is admitted
tasks.change: Emit the parent replenishment cue for the actual accepted replacement, not a generic every-round supply message.
tasks.acceptance: No message promises a resource that was denied by the active arena budget or eligibility rule.
tasks.forbidden: Do not increase supply quantity to make the message true.

tasks.title: A shared challenge code reproduces the rules, not just the random seed
tasks.distinct_delta: Seed, records and replay work already exist. This is a compatibility contract for a local challenge/attempt comparison across content changes, without adding accounts or online leaderboards.
mechanism: Extend the existing run/challenge envelope with its actual ruleset/content compatibility identifier and the starting fit/mutators required for reproduction.
Reuse current replay/records storage to distinguish a comparable attempt from an older incompatible one; a seed alone must not be represented as exact replay proof.
Import a compact bounded code through the existing normal setup route, validate it without mutating the running save, and leave incompatible records viewable as history rather than deleting them.
tasks.route: Finish a normal Crucible attempt, copy its existing challenge/share code, start another attempt from it, then import a deliberately old ruleset code.
acceptance: Same compatible envelope produces the same planned opening and declared starting conditions.
Invalid or oversized codes leave the current game and records intact.
Incompatible attempts are labeled non-comparable instead of being silently ranked or replayed under new rules.
tasks.non_goals: No cloud service, public leaderboard, authentication system, cross-version determinism promise or new replay engine.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Reject an invalid challenge seed before starting a run
tasks.change: Keep the planner's finite integer seed bounds on imported values, including strings coerced by the setup surface.
tasks.acceptance: Zero, out-of-range, NaN and malformed seeds produce a setup error without partial run creation.
tasks.forbidden: Do not silently clamp every invalid seed to one.

tasks.title: A canceled retry leaves the finished record unchanged
tasks.change: Keep preview/retry navigation read-only until the current run owner accepts a new run request.
tasks.acceptance: Open retry, cancel, reopen results: the finished attempt is still complete and identical.
tasks.forbidden: Do not mutate record timestamps as a UI refresh.

tasks.title: Label a ruleset mismatch without discarding the score
tasks.change: Expose the parent compatibility result alongside existing attempt metadata.
tasks.acceptance: An older result remains readable but is not presented as directly comparable to the current challenge.
tasks.forbidden: Do not overwrite historical scores with recalculated values.

tasks.title: Round-trip mutators in stable order in the challenge code
tasks.change: Canonicalize the parent permitted mutator list for export/import while rejecting unsupported entries.
tasks.acceptance: Equivalent supported sets produce the same envelope; an unknown mutator is reported instead of silently ignored.
tasks.forbidden: Do not sort authoritative simulation entities.

tasks.title: Deep-core mining makes the next commitment visible without revealing the whole rock
tasks.distinct_delta: Drill heat, energy, gas tells, scan pulses and persistent tunnels already exist. This packet turns those known facts into a local commitment decision, without changing ore tiers or generating a second mining game.
mechanism: Derive the next reachable drilling decision from the current revealed field, bit tier, energy, heat and cargo room.
Show only the available local evidence: known ore, suspected gas, blocked tier and the path back through cleared cells. Never reveal unscanned cells or promise unknown yield.
Reconcile the chosen bite/hold cadence with accepted extraction so a careful tap remains meaningful and repeated tapping cannot create free work.
tasks.route: Enter a normally reachable drill lens, scan once, choose between a safe nearby vein and a deeper risky known vein, retreat and return to the same rock.
acceptance: The decision view distinguishes known facts from unrevealed territory.
Tap/hold outcomes retain the current bore-debt and energy rules rather than granting extra mining work.
Re-entry preserves the appropriate depletion/tunnel history and does not replenish cargo yield through a UI reset.
tasks.non_goals: No new mining currency, full-map scanner, depth-based ore-tier rewrite, endless popup tutorial or separate resource simulation.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: A tier-blocked vein names the required existing head tier
tasks.change: Use drillTierReqForOre/current tier data for the refusal label instead of depth or a generic cannot-drill message.
tasks.acceptance: The same ore reports the same requirement at two depths; unknown ore is not guessed.
tasks.forbidden: Do not rebalance the tier catalog.

tasks.title: A depleted rock does not animate a successful cargo grant
tasks.change: Emit extraction success only for the accepted positive yield while retaining the physical bore feedback.
tasks.acceptance: A cleared but exhausted cell can still show drilling work without claiming ore entered the hold.
tasks.forbidden: Do not refill the rock to make the effect pay.

tasks.title: Mark the known return path without tracing through unknown cells
tasks.change: Use the parent revealed/cleared-cell projection for the existing cable/return display.
tasks.acceptance: The displayed route follows actual known cells and reveals no hidden gas or ore.
tasks.forbidden: Do not add autopilot through the grid.

tasks.title: Explain energy exhaustion separately from overheating
tasks.change: Present the parent local limitation using its actual energy/heat state and current recovery threshold.
tasks.acceptance: The player can distinguish wait-for-energy from cool-the-bit without inspecting diagnostics.
tasks.forbidden: Do not merge both into an invented stamina meter.

tasks.title: Extraction never loses material merely because the hold fills mid-bite
tasks.distinct_delta: Pickup acceptance and cargo ownership already have helpers. This packet applies their accepted-quantity law consistently to beam mining, drill yield and physical chunks during a capacity change.
mechanism: At each extraction commit, distinguish material freed from material actually accepted by cargo.
Preserve the unaccepted material in the existing rock/chunk/remaining-yield representation appropriate to that verb; do not subtract it from the rock and then silently discard it.
Let ordinary collection, jettison and return recover the remainder, while keeping field depletion and cargo mass caches consistent.
tasks.route: Mine with room for less than one normal payout, fill the hold during a bite, dump a selected legal lot and return for the remaining material using both beam and drill routes.
acceptance: Freed material equals accepted cargo plus recoverable remainder plus explicitly caused destruction.
Full-hold retries cannot duplicate yield or reset depletion.
Partial acceptance updates mass/volume once and does not block on mass as a second capacity.
tasks.non_goals: No automatic inventory expansion, magic overflow wallet, free ore refund detached from the source or replacement mining system.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: Use the accepted amount in the mining pickup cue
tasks.change: Pass successfulPickupAmount/accepted quantity to the existing cargo pickup feedback rather than the requested ore amount.
tasks.acceptance: A request for five with room for two reports two accepted, not five.
tasks.forbidden: Do not increase the pickup radius or hold size.

tasks.title: Keep a full-hold refusal on its existing retry cadence
tasks.change: Retain the current bounded retry delay for capacity refusal so a nearby full hold does not emit a result every tick.
tasks.acceptance: Standing beside rejected material produces bounded retries and collection resumes promptly after capacity is freed.
tasks.forbidden: Do not permanently blacklist the material after one refusal.

tasks.title: Return drill overflow to the same source accounting
tasks.change: Apply the parent unaccepted-yield disposition without creating a new unrelated ore grant on exit.
tasks.acceptance: Exit and re-enter after partial acceptance: only the remaining source budget is available.
tasks.forbidden: Do not restore all drilled tiles to create a refund.

tasks.title: Do not decrement depletion twice for a retried remainder
tasks.change: Recognize the parent extraction identity when a previously freed remainder is finally collected.
tasks.acceptance: Collection after capacity is freed changes cargo but does not charge the rock for the same extraction again.
tasks.forbidden: Do not suppress genuinely new extraction events.

tasks.title: A congested receiver offers a physical sorting job with a real throughput consequence
tasks.distinct_delta: Moving intakes, shape jams and full depots already have plans. This packet chooses a complete production bottleneck: sort the obstructing load into its valid destination and watch the backed-up work resume.
mechanism: Select one existing receiver where two valid cargo classes contend for a finite intake/output condition.
Represent blockage using its actual stored goods, load geometry or machine state, and expose two existing physical interventions: remove the obstruction or redirect the next appropriate load.
On successful intervention, let the same worker/receiver cycle resume and consume the correct input; the reward follows real accepted work rather than a parallel mission flag.
tasks.route: Arrive at the chosen normal industrial site while it is backed up, identify the obstructing load, sort it with Massline and observe at least one resumed delivery.
acceptance: The named obstruction is both visible and causally sufficient for the stopped work.
A valid intervention changes receiver throughput and the waiting worker's next action.
Sorting the wrong class cannot complete the job, destroy its identity or pay repeatedly.
tasks.non_goals: No new factory-builder mode, scripted conveyor teleport, extra worker crowd or reward for merely touching a marker.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: A receiver names the current missing condition
tasks.change: Prefer the actual blockage/input/output condition in the existing operation refusal result.
tasks.acceptance: Empty input, full output and blocked geometry are distinguishable causes.
tasks.forbidden: Do not create three separate popups for one refusal.

tasks.title: Do not consume the wrong commodity on a valid contact
tasks.change: Validate the existing operation's accepted material class before removing cargo or completing work.
tasks.acceptance: A physically correct delivery of the wrong good leaves both inventories unchanged.
tasks.forbidden: Do not silently transmute the good to fit the recipe.

tasks.title: Resume the waiting worker at its real next stage
tasks.change: Consume the parent receiver-unblocked result without resetting the worker's route or manufacturing a new load.
tasks.acceptance: After sorting, the same worker continues the same shipment.
tasks.forbidden: Do not respawn a fresh decorative worker.

tasks.title: Keep the emptied obstruction interactable as ordinary salvage
tasks.change: After the parent blocked load is resolved, retain any legitimate remaining body under its normal lifecycle and ownership.
tasks.acceptance: Clearing the job does not despawn a still-useful player-manipulated object.
tasks.forbidden: Do not preserve meaningless debris forever.

tasks.title: Repair consumes delivered materials and preserves unfinished work
tasks.distinct_delta: Repair and site persistence are existing foundations. This extension specifies a two-stage material-backed repair that can be left, resumed and interrupted without consuming the same inputs twice.
mechanism: Choose one current repairable machine; split its existing operation into a material admission stage and a work-progress stage only if its owner already supports such phases.
Admit real delivered repair goods through cargo/site owners, retain the accepted work receipt, and resume from that durable state after leaving or loading.
Restore only the repaired function and its operating visual state; partial repair remains useful evidence rather than resetting the whole machine or paying the final reward early.
tasks.route: At the selected normal worksite, deliver part of the repair input, perform some work, leave or save/load, then return with the remainder and finish.
acceptance: Each accepted material unit is consumed once across interruption and resume.
The machine's working capability changes only at the appropriate accepted stage.
An abandoned partial job leaves coherent site state and a reachable next action, not a permanent busy lock.
tasks.non_goals: No new crafting economy, progress by wall-clock offline time, direct credit/cargo writes or visual repair that leaves the actual machinery broken.
tasks.budget: Reuse the existing owner and bounded record lifetime. No new per-frame universe scan, persistent decorative entities, or extra full-state copy. Report any changed entity/query/voice/draw count before claiming a performance-neutral result.

tasks.title: A partial repair result names what is still missing
tasks.change: Return the existing accepted amount and remaining requirement after a partial material admission.
tasks.acceptance: A half delivery reports the actual remaining goods instead of repeating the original full requirement.
tasks.forbidden: Do not change recipe cost as a copy fix.

tasks.title: A canceled operation releases only its own busy state
tasks.change: Clear the current operation's transient activity token on cancellation without clearing other site work.
tasks.acceptance: Canceling one repair cannot stop an unrelated receiver operation or leave the repaired machine permanently reserved.
tasks.forbidden: Do not reset the entire site runtime.

tasks.title: Describe the retained repair stage after returning
tasks.change: Expose the parent durable material/work stage through the existing site readout.
tasks.acceptance: Return after load shows previously accepted materials and the real next action, not a fresh-start prompt.
tasks.forbidden: Do not replay the original completion cue on restore.

tasks.title: Keep a repaired function independent of unrelated damage
tasks.change: For the selected parent site, bind the restored operating state to the repaired function rather than a blanket pristine variant.
tasks.acceptance: Completing this repair does not erase another accepted damage/scar state at the same site.
